title: Gideon and the Letter
premise: Estate lawyer Ada Halloran is hired to read the will of Marguerite Voss, a woman who vanished eleven years ago and was declared dead — yet the will was drafted three years after her disappearance, in handwriting that matches her own. When Ada discovers Marguerite's diary continues past the date she vanished, she realizes someone has been writing as a dead woman for a decade, and that three 'accidental' deaths among the estate's beneficiaries were anything but. With the help of disgraced former detective Gideon Marsh, Ada sets a trap using the will itself as bait, forcing the killer to reveal how deeply they've infiltrated the case file. In the end, Ada must choose between exposing a truth that destroys an innocent family's inheritance or burying it — and she finds a third path: justice outside the law, paid for with the letter Marguerite left behind.
about_author: D. M. Halloran is the pen name of a former probate clerk who spent fifteen years reading other people's last words before starting to write them. They live near the coast, where fog makes everything look like evidence.

chapters.title: The Will That Shouldn't Exist
chapters.summary: Ada Halloran, POV. Ada is summoned to read the will of Marguerite Voss, declared dead eleven years ago, only to find the document dated three years after the disappearance. The paper is authentic; the signature matches. Emotional beat: professional unease curdling into obsession as Ada realizes the law has already closed this case once.

chapters.title: Beneficiaries of a Ghost
chapters.summary: Ada, POV. The will names four heirs, two already dead in accidents the police ruled clean. Ada interviews the surviving pair — the brittle widow Corinne Voss and the family accountant, Elias Brandt — who both seem rehearsed. Emotional beat: creeping dread beneath polite drawing-room conversation.

chapters.title: Gideon
chapters.summary: Gideon Marsh, POV. Gideon, the detective who originally declared Marguerite dead and lost his career over doubts he never voiced, receives an anonymous note quoting his own suppressed report verbatim. He seeks out Ada. Emotional beat: wary recognition between two people who each know the file too well.

chapters.title: Pages Past the End
chapters.summary: Ada, POV. In the estate archive Ada finds Marguerite's diary — and entries continuing for ten years after the disappearance date, in the same hand, describing ordinary days. Someone alive has been writing as a dead woman. Emotional beat: vertigo; the ground truth of the case dissolves.

chapters.title: Three Accidents
chapters.summary: Gideon, POV. Gideon reopens the two deaths: a fall from the boathouse stairs, a carbon monoxide leak. Both victims had recently asked questions about Marguerite. The third beneficiary, Marguerite's brother Thomas, died before the will was ever read. Emotional beat: cold clarity — this is a pattern, not chance.

chapters.title: The House Remembers
chapters.summary: Ada, POV. Ada stays overnight at Voss House to examine the study where the will was drafted. She finds ink matching the diary under a blotter and hears someone moving through the east wing at night. Emotional beat: isolation sharpening into fear inside a house full of locked rooms.

chapters.title: What Corinne Knew
chapters.summary: Ada, POV. Corinne admits Marguerite planned to change her will the week she vanished — cutting everyone out in favor of an unnamed charity. Corinne swears she never saw her sister-in-law again. Her hands shake too much for a liar. Emotional beat: pity complicating suspicion.

chapters.title: The Case File Better Than Ours
chapters.summary: Gideon, POV. Someone mails Gideon pages of the original investigation file that were never copied — including his private margin notes. Whoever it is had access to the evidence room for years. Emotional beat: violation; the hunter realizing he has been observed all along.

chapters.title: Elias's Ledger
chapters.summary: Ada, POV. Ada confronts accountant Elias Brandt about irregular transfers from the estate — small monthly payments to a 'consultant' dating back a decade. Elias deflects beautifully, then warns her off with a smile. Emotional beat: the pleasure of a sharp exchange shadowed by real menace.

chapters.title: Marguerite's Letter
chapters.summary: Ada, POV. Hidden in the diary's binding, Ada finds a sealed letter addressed 'To whoever reads past my last page.' It names no killer but describes a threat so precise that Marguerite faked her death to escape it. Emotional beat: intimacy with a stranger across eleven years; grief for the living.

chapters.title: Thomas's Daughter
chapters.summary: Gideon, POV. Gideon tracks down Nina, Thomas Voss's estranged daughter, who inherited nothing and resents it. She reveals Thomas received letters from Marguerite after the disappearance — meaning she lived, hidden, until at least eight years ago. Emotional beat: anger giving way to alliance.

chapters.title: The Consultant
chapters.summary: Ada, POV. Following the ledger payments, Ada reaches a shuttered records office and learns the consultant's identity is shielded by a trust she herself once helped draft — someone used her own legal work as camouflage. Emotional beat: humiliation and fury; the trap was built with her tools.

chapters.title: Dead Air
chapters.summary: Gideon, POV. Gideon's anonymous correspondent goes silent, then sends one line: 'Stop looking for her. She found peace.' Attached is a recent photograph of the boathouse — taken hours ago. Emotional beat: escalation; the watcher stepping into the open.

chapters.title: Corinne's Confession, Almost
chapters.summary: Ada, POV. Pressed by Ada, Corinne breaks down: she knew Marguerite was alive, received money to stay quiet, and believes Marguerite died two years ago — because the diary entries stopped being true. The details went wrong. Emotional beat: sorrow; a witness drowning in complicity.

chapters.title: Forged Days
chapters.summary: Ada, POV. Ada forensically compares the diary and proves the final three years of entries are forged by a different hand imitating Marguerite's — written to keep the death declaration valid and the estate frozen. The forger needed the will unread. Until now. Emotional beat: triumph inverted — solving it means springing it.

chapters.title: Bait
chapters.summary: Gideon and Ada, alternating POV. They announce a formal reading of the will for Friday, leaking that the diary will be entered as evidence. Their plan: let the forger come destroy it. Emotional beat: taut resolve, and the unspoken fear that they are bait too.

chapters.title: The Reading
chapters.summary: Ada, POV. At the reading, every suspect gathers. Ada reads the will aloud and watches faces instead of listening to words. When she mentions the diary, one person's stillness gives them away — Elias Brandt, whose rehearsed calm finally cracks. Emotional beat: quiet detonation in a room pretending to be ordinary.

chapters.title: Boathouse
chapters.summary: Gideon, POV. That night the diary is stolen from the estate safe, and Gideon follows the trail to the boathouse where the first accident happened. He interrupts Elias burning the diary and is attacked; Ada arrives having anticipated the move. Emotional beat: violence breaking through the mystery's surface.

chapters.title: How He Did It
chapters.summary: Ada, POV. Cornered, Elias confesses: he discovered Marguerite hiding abroad, blackmailed her for years, killed her when she tried to end it, and forged the diary to preserve the estate he was bleeding. The accidents were beneficiaries who got close. Emotional beat: revulsion at banal greed wearing a careful face.

chapters.title: Outside the Law
chapters.summary: Ada and Gideon, alternating POV. The confession is unusable — obtained illegally, backed by evidence Elias burned. The police can hold him only briefly. Ada and Gideon must decide whether to hand him to a system that failed Marguerite twice. Emotional beat: moral weight; loyalty to truth against loyalty to procedure.

chapters.title: The Third Path
chapters.summary: Ada, POV. Ada uses the trust documents and Elias's own ledger to legally strip him of everything, while Gideon feeds the confession to a journalist and a federal prosecutor untainted by the original file. Elias is ruined and hunted properly. Marguerite's letter is finally honored. Emotional beat: hard-won satisfaction, justice neither clean nor lawful but real.

chapters.title: Last Page
chapters.summary: Ada, POV. Weeks later, Ada closes the estate. Nina inherits what remains; Corinne keeps the house and her freedom. Ada files the diary's true final page — Marguerite's own words about choosing to disappear — and writes her resignation letter, then doesn't send it. Emotional beat: bittersweet peace; some inheritances are burdens you choose to carry.
